tasks.short: Create playlists tailored to event functions.

steps.what: Understand actual event functions, audience needs and music constraints
Select and sequence music aligned with actual event functions
outputs: actual chosen tracks and event sequence

steps.what: Create tailored playlists in the DJ library software {OTHER} from chosen tracks
inputs: actual chosen tracks and event sequence
actual track identifiers and event labels

steps.what: Check final tailored playlists against the actual event brief and chosen sequence
inputs: actual chosen tracks and event sequence

steps.what: Save the checked final tailored event playlists

tasks.design: Configure native event crates, selected-track import and reusable labels in the DJ library software {OTHER}, using actual brief information from {CRM} and {DOCS}. The DJ chooses music and sequence and checks the final tailored playlists before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Building an already chosen playlist can repeat track lookup and event labels.
tasks.enabler_now: Native selected-track and crate functions can reduce repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Audience fit, mood and sequencing require musical and event judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The DJ understands why a track fits one event function but disrupts another.
tasks.altitude: Less playlist entry; musical direction stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native DJ-library crates and selected-track import can reduce repeated playlist entry; they do not establish musical suitability.

assumptions: Actual event owner supplies agreed brief, functions and restrictions. DJ interprets them in s1 and selects actual track identifiers and sequence in s2; missing versions and labels remain manual in s3.
Cuts cover repeated entry after musical choice, not listening, selection or sequencing. Native functions first; already quick drag-and-drop or configured imports earn zero new saving.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Save remains one percent and uses the existing final playlist check. Actual event playback or external sharing is a separate action with no saving claimed here.
unknowns: Which playlist fields are actually entered repeatedly?
research_questions: Does native selected-track reuse reduce preparation after full musical selection?

incremental.description: Maintain actual event crate and label defaults.

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final tailored playlists and exact event crate destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 30*0.50 repeated playlist entry = 15; minus 1 upkeep = 14. Half eligible gives 7.5 minus 1 = 6.5. Event interpretation, music choice, check and save stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Listen to recordings for suitability and quality.

steps.what: Listen to music before events to assess actual appropriateness and recording quality
outputs: actual heard suitability and quality findings

steps.what: Enter and check actual listening findings in existing DJ library quality tags {OTHER}
inputs: actual heard suitability and quality findings

steps.what: Save the checked final actual listening tags

tasks.design: Use native selected-track context and existing quality-tag fields in the DJ library software {OTHER}. The DJ still listens to the recordings and supplies the actual suitability and quality findings before checking and saving tags.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing listening notes may repeat track references and tag entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native selected-track tags can reduce reference entry.
tasks.still_hard: Audible defects, content and event appropriateness require actual listening.
tasks.human_edge: The DJ hears issues and context that file metadata cannot establish.
tasks.altitude: Less existing tag entry; listening remains fully retained.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native track tags can retain actual listening findings; metadata does not establish audible quality or suitability.

assumptions: DJ listens in s1 and captures actual findings in retained s2; the library supplies actual track identifier and version only. No automated listening or free note capture is assumed.
Only an existing listening-tag practice is eligible. If no record exists, omit s2/s3 and reweight listening to 100: zero saving. No new record-keeping baseline is invented.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Existing native context earns no saving. Routine save remains one percent and uses the existing final tag check.
unknowns: Does tag entry repeat track references?
research_questions: Can existing selected-track tags reduce entry without shortening listening?

approvals.approved_version: s2 checked final actual listening tags and exact track/version destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 9*0.30 tag references = 2.7; minus 0.5 upkeep = 2.2. Half eligible gives 1.35 minus 0.5 = 0.85. All listening and routine save stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Retrieve actual music files, playlist entries and existing metadata
Choose actual music-library categories, playlist organisation and ambiguous version handling
outputs: actual chosen organisation rules and exceptions

steps.what: Organize music libraries or playlists with native tags and filtered crates {OTHER}
inputs: actual chosen organisation rules and exceptions
outputs: draft organised music library and playlists

steps.what: Check final library organisation, duplicate flags and actual track-version distinctions
inputs: draft organised music library and playlists
actual chosen organisation rules and exceptions
outputs: checked final organised library and playlists

steps.what: Commit the checked final library organisation and playlists
inputs: checked final organised library and playlists

tasks.design: Configure native metadata imports, tags and filtered crates in the DJ library software {OTHER}. The DJ chooses organisation rules, resolves ambiguous versions and checks the final organisation before committing changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Library organisation may repeat metadata copying and membership edits.
tasks.enabler_now: Native metadata import and explicit crate rules can reduce repeated edits.
tasks.still_hard: Version distinctions and useful musical categories need actual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The DJ knows which edits and versions should remain distinct for performance.
tasks.altitude: Less library maintenance; musical categorisation stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native DJ-library metadata imports and filtered crates can reduce manual organisation; ambiguous versions still require checking.

assumptions: Actual file metadata and identifiers already exist; DJ checks source fields in s1 and supplies missing labels/rules in retained s2/s3. No automatic inference of mood or free metadata cleaning is assumed.
No deletion, audio replacement or external publication is introduced. Duplicate flags are suggestions and actual versions remain checked in s4.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Only repeated source and membership entry is eligible; existing automatic crates earn zero saving. Commit retains one percent and uses the existing final organisation check.
If library metadata also supports tailored playlists, count its capture and upkeep once in any combined estimate.
unknowns: Which native imports and crates are already used?
How many metadata fields require manual judgement?
research_questions: Can explicit native rules reduce membership edits while retaining distinct versions?

incremental.description: Maintain actual library metadata mappings and crate rules.

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final organisation and exact library/playlist destinations; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15*0.50 source entry + 35*0.50 organisation edits = 25; minus 1 upkeep = 24. Half eligible gives 12.5 minus 1 = 11.5. Musical rules, final check and commit stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create itemised invoices for completed DJ services.

steps.what: Retrieve and verify actual completed services, agreed rates, expenses and billing details
inputs: actual authorised expenses and billing identity

steps.what: Calculate actual item amounts, totals and applicable invoice charges
inputs: actual approved tax and charge rules

steps.what: Create itemized invoices to record amounts due for actual services rendered
Check final invoice against actual completed services, agreed charges and billing identity
Commit the checked final itemised service invoice

tasks.design: Configure native completed-booking field reuse from {CRM} and invoice calculations/templates in {ERP}. The DJ verifies actual service completion and charges, checks the final itemised invoice and separately commits the amount due.
tasks.previous_blocker: Invoices may repeat completed booking fields, arithmetic and line formatting.
tasks.enabler_now: Native booking references, fixed calculations and invoice templates can remove actual duplication.
tasks.still_hard: Service completion, agreed extras and correct billing identity require verification.
tasks.human_edge: The DJ knows what was actually delivered and whether a charge was agreed.
tasks.altitude: Less invoice preparation; charge approval stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native accounting invoice calculations and templates can reuse actual completed-booking fields; booking plans alone do not prove services were rendered.

assumptions: Actual booking owner records completed service, date, quantity/hours and agreed rates after the event; actual expense evidence and customer billing fields already exist. DJ verifies completeness and actual approved tax/charge rules in retained s1, capturing missing inputs manually.
No free event-completion capture or legal tax determination is assumed. Native accounting configuration first; already automated invoices and formula runtime earn zero saving.
Boundary is creating and recording the invoice. Any customer send is a separate final-version-gated delivery, with no labour saving claimed here.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Routine commit remains one percent and uses the existing final invoice check.
unknowns: Which completed booking fields are copied?
Are invoice totals already calculated automatically?
research_questions: Does native completed-booking reuse reduce entry after actual delivery and charge verification?

incremental.description: Maintain actual booking/invoice field mappings, rates and templates.

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final itemised invoice and exact customer accounting destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.50 source entry + 20 arithmetic + 30*0.50 invoice lines = 45; minus 1.5 upkeep = 43.5. Half eligible gives 22.5 minus 1.5 = 21. Actual completion/charge checking and commit stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: DJs retain musical judgement and actual listening while native library organisation and completed-booking invoicing can reduce repeated preparation.
skills_to_grow: Native DJ-library rules and metadata checks
role.ambitious_version: Validate actual repeated entry, preserving listening, musical choices and charge verification.
